summary.text: Democrat Susie Lee represents Nevada's 3rd District, was first elected in 2018, and won re-election on November 3, 2026. Born in Canton, Ohio, and educated at Carnegie Mellon University, she moved to Las Vegas in 1993 and worked as a policy advisor and in education and homelessness nonprofits before entering Congress. She sits on the House Appropriations Committee, and her official biography describes her as a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus and the New Democrats Coalition.

paragraphs.text: Lee was born in Canton, Ohio, in 1966. Her official biography says she was born into a working family of ten and that her father, a military veteran, worked at a steel plant.

She earned a bachelor's degree in policy and management in 1989 and a master's degree in public policy and management in 1990, both from Carnegie Mellon University; her official biography says she worked her way through with scholarships, loans and part-time jobs. She then worked at an environmental and economic consulting firm in Massachusetts that specialized in water resource issues.
Lee moved to Las Vegas in 1993, where she worked as a campaign policy advisor to Las Vegas Mayor Jan Laverty Jones and founded a homeless shelter for parents and children in need.

Her official biography says she became a leader in education nonprofits in Las Vegas, founding After School All Stars and later serving as president of Communities In Schools of Nevada, a program aimed at lowering high school dropout rates; Ballotpedia dates her time as board president from 2010.
Lee was elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and re-elected in 2020, 2022 (52.0% to 48.0%) and 2024 (51.4% to 48.6%).

In 2025-2026 she serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Energy and Water Development, and Defense subcommittees) and the Natural Resources Committee; earlier terms included Education and the Workforce, Veterans' Affairs and other Appropriations subcommittees.

Her official biography says she has led bipartisan legislation signed into law on housing costs, Nevada's water supply, access to health care, online child exploitation and veterans' health care. It also says she is Battleground Leadership Representative in the Democratic Caucus, a position she created in 2022, and that she lives in Las Vegas and has two children.
She won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 59.6% of the vote to Marty O'Donnell's 38.1% and Jon Kamerath's 2.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
